content.text: Section 17.8 describes what the Eduversal School Appraisal does. This section records what it is built on, and why its five domains do not copy any single external framework. The distinction matters because the appraisal is regularly asked to serve two audiences at once: an Eduversal Subject Specialist calibrating a rating across fifteen schools, and a school leader assembling evidence for CIS, WASC or BAN-S/M accreditation. Without a written mapping, the second audience has to reconstruct the connection by eye, and every school reconstructs it differently.

The Eduversal School Appraisal Framework is a deliberate synthesis. It draws on international accreditation practice (CIS, WASC, NEASC), on Cambridge's own school-quality expectations, and on the Indonesian legal frameworks that bind every partner school (BAN-S/M IASP 2020 and the principal competency standards). No single one of these is the parent framework. Where they agree, our domains follow them. Where they diverge, our domains follow what is defensible in an Indonesian Cambridge school — which is sometimes none of them exactly.
Three cautions on how to read the mapping tables that follow.

items: A mapping is a correspondence, not an equivalence. "D2 maps to WASC Category B" means evidence gathered for one is substantially usable for the other — not that a strong D2 rating satisfies WASC Category B, and not that the two ask identical questions.

The mapping is many-to-many. Our five domains cover CIS's nine and WASC's five, so most of our domains answer to more than one external domain, and several external domains are split across two of ours.

An accreditation body judges its own framework. Nothing in this section is a claim about accreditation outcomes. A school pursuing CIS or WASC still completes that body's own self-study; the appraisal reduces the evidence-gathering burden, it does not substitute for the process.

content.text: The framework rates 31 aspects across five domains, each aspect on a 1-4 scale (Beginning / Developing / Established / Exemplary) with band descriptors written for that aspect rather than a generic scale. The domains:

items: D1 — Leadership & Governance (5 aspects): vision and strategic direction, SMART goals and the P.I.E. model, leadership structure and shared leadership, performance management and staff KPIs, governance and transparent decision-making

D2 — Teaching & Learning Quality (6 aspects): in-class documents and observation records, assessment methods, student understanding and goal setting, assessment and feedback quality, evaluation of teaching and PD records, LMS and technology integration

D3 — Curriculum & Academic Programmes (8 aspects): department structure, department meetings and HoD coordination, teacher self-assessment, formal observations and walkthroughs, mentoring and peer observation, PD evaluation, cultural and authentic contexts, digital policy

D4 — Student Achievement & Learning Outcomes (6 aspects): achievement data and dashboards, Olympiad resourcing and academic follow-up, Olympiad student wellbeing, support for advanced students, language support, identification of and support for additional learning needs

D5 — School Culture & Community (6 aspects): culture, climate and student behaviour, safeguarding and child protection, communication structures, educational and co-curricular programmes, parent and community engagement, staff wellbeing

content.text: Each domain is owned by two Domain Leads who hold rating consistency across the network. The pair is always split across a school's two visits, so full domain coverage comes from the pairing rather than from repeat visits by one person.

CIS assesses against nine domains (see Section 18.2 for the full list). Its evaluation is process-oriented — "how do we operate as an organisation?" — and its self-study plus peer-review visit is the structural model the Eduversal appraisal follows most closely.

items: CIS 1 Purpose and Direction -> D1 (vision, mission, strategic planning). CIS also expects Schoolwide Learning Outcomes here; see 24.7.
CIS 2 Governance and Leadership -> D1 (leadership structure, governance, transparent decision-making)
CIS 3 Curriculum -> D3 (curriculum delivery, departmental organisation, resources)
CIS 4 Teaching and Learning -> D2 (classroom practice, differentiation, technology in learning)
CIS 5 Assessment -> D2 (assessment methods, feedback quality) and D4 (achievement data, reporting)
CIS 6 Student Wellbeing -> D5 (safeguarding, culture, behaviour) and D4 (language support, additional learning needs)
CIS 7 Staffing -> D1 (performance management) and D3 (mentoring, peer observation, PD evaluation)
CIS 8 Premises and Resources -> D3 (learning resources) and D5 (facilities as they bear on culture). Financial and facilities management sit largely outside our scope; see 24.8.
CIS 9 Community and Partnerships -> D5 (parent and community engagement)

content.text: What Eduversal takes from CIS structurally: mandatory self-study before the visit, a visiting team drawn from outside the school, commendations paired with recommendations, an assigned continuity figure (the CIS Visiting Team Leader is the precedent for our Visit I Supervisor), and a formal appeal route.

subsections.title: WASC — ACS WASC FOCUS ON LEARNING

content.text: The relevant WASC framework for partner schools is the ACS WASC "Focus on Learning" (FOL) model for K-12 schools — not the Postsecondary framework, which applies to colleges and universities. FOL is more outcome-oriented than CIS: it asks what impact school practices have on student learning. Its five categories:

items: Category A Organization for Student Learning -> D1 (vision, governance, leadership, resource alignment)
Category B Curriculum, Instruction, and Assessment -> D2 and D3 (standards-based curriculum, instructional quality, assessment systems, use of data)
Category C Support for Student Personal and Academic Growth -> D4 (language support, additional learning needs, advanced students) and D5 (pastoral care, wellbeing)
Category D Resource Management and Development -> partially D3 (learning resources) and D5 (facilities, staff wellbeing). Financial resourcing is out of scope; see 24.8.

Category E Focus on Learning — the schoolwide action plan -> the appraisal's own action-plan cycle: the school responds to recommendations within four weeks, and progress is reviewed at the Phase 2 mid-year check-in and in the following cycle

content.text: What Eduversal takes from WASC: the self-study plus visiting-committee validation model, and the discipline of judging practices by their effect on learning rather than by their existence on paper. WASC's separation of a Focus Visit (instructional quality) from a Full Visit (whole institutional system) is the precedent for splitting our cycle into a Phase 1 Teaching Quality Visit and a Phase 3 Validation Visit.

NEASC's ACE (Accreditation for Curriculum Effectiveness) model rates schools against learner-centred principles rather than compliance checklists. Eduversal draws one specific thing from it: the insistence that a quality judgement must reach the student's actual experience of learning, not stop at the systems intended to produce it.

items: ACE learning principles -> D4 (Student Achievement & Learning Outcomes) carries this most directly, and is the reason D4 exists as a domain in its own right rather than as a sub-section of D2
ACE foundation standards -> D1 (governance and strategic direction) and D5 (culture and community as the conditions for learning)
The NEASC School Liaison Officer, who manages the self-study relationship across the cycle, is a second precedent for our paired supervisor model

subsections.title: INDONESIAN FRAMEWORKS — IASP 2020 AND PRINCIPAL COMPETENCY STANDARDS

content.text: BAN-S/M (Badan Akreditasi Nasional Sekolah/Madrasah) accredits Indonesian schools against the IASP 2020 instrument (Instrumen Akreditasi Satuan Pendidikan). Unlike CIS and WASC, this is not optional: it is the legal accreditation framework, and partner schools are subject to it whatever their Cambridge status. IASP 2020 has four components:

items: Mutu Lulusan (graduate quality) -> D4 (achievement data, learning outcomes) and D5 (student behaviour and character)
Proses Pembelajaran (learning process) -> D2 (classroom practice, assessment, feedback)
Mutu Guru (teacher quality) -> D2 (evaluation of teaching) and D3 (PD, mentoring, peer observation, department structures)
Manajemen Sekolah (school management) -> D1 (leadership, governance, performance management) and D5 (communication, parent engagement)

content.text: The practical consequence: evidence assembled for an Eduversal appraisal is substantially the evidence an IASP visit asks for, and the Phase 3 Validation Visit can be run as an IASP-readiness audit. The reverse does not hold — IASP does not ask about Cambridge programme implementation, Olympiad provision, or EAL support at the depth D3 and D4 require.

Indonesian competency standards are carried on the appraisal domains as PMD tags, so that staff development and school appraisal cross-walk rather than running as unrelated judgements. NOTE a known inconsistency here, flagged 2026-07-29 and not yet resolved: the PMD chip family resolves against Permendiknas No. 16/2007 (Standar Kualifikasi Akademik dan Kompetensi Guru — the four TEACHER pillars: pedagogik, profesional, sosial, kepribadian), and the frameworkAnchors on D2/D3/D4 tag those teacher pillars. But D1 and D5 tag 'Kompetensi Manajerial', 'Kompetensi Kewirausahaan' and 'Kompetensi Sosial' / 'Kepribadian', which belong to Permendiknas No. 13/2007 (Standar Kepala Sekolah/Madrasah — the five PRINCIPAL competencies). The two regulations are being tagged under one chip family, and 13/2007 is not in the research archive, so the manajerial and kewirausahaan chips currently resolve to nothing.

items: Currently tagged, resolving via 16/2007 (teacher pillars): Kompetensi Pedagogik -> D2, D3 · Kompetensi Profesional -> D2, D3, D4 · Kompetensi Sosial -> D5 · Kompetensi Kepribadian -> D5
Currently tagged, NOT resolving (13/2007 principal competencies, absent from the archive): Kompetensi Manajerial -> D1 · Kompetensi Kewirausahaan -> D1
Not tagged anywhere: Kompetensi Supervisi (13/2007), which would map naturally to D2 and D3

Resolution requires a decision: either archive 13/2007 and split PMD into two chip families (teacher vs principal), or drop the principal competencies from the appraisal tags and carry them only on principal appraisal. Do not silently rewrite the tags to fit the existing chip family — that would hide a real gap in the Indonesian legal mapping.

content.text: Safeguarding within D5 answers to Permendikdasmen 6/2026 (Budaya Sekolah Aman dan Nyaman), which revoked Permendikbudristek 46/2023 PPKSP on 9 January 2026. SPK schools running Cambridge are in scope. See Section 9 for the operational detail; note in particular that 6/2026 makes the kepala sekolah the singular accountable officer and fixes no statutory reporting timeframe.

Cambridge International publishes both a school self-evaluation expectation and the Cambridge School Leader Standards (CSLS 2023, 25 standards across 5 areas). CSLS refs are carried on every appraisal domain, visible as CSLS chips in the domain headers, so that a leadership development conversation and a school appraisal rating point at the same standard rather than at two vocabularies.

Cambridge programme implementation — syllabus coverage, centre obligations, examinations administration — is assessed through D3, but the authoritative detail sits in Sections 3 and 10 rather than in the appraisal framework.
The mapping is honest about where it does not reach. Four divergences are deliberate and should be stated to any school using the appraisal as accreditation preparation.

items: Schoolwide Learning Outcomes. Both CIS and WASC place SLOs at the centre — WASC's entire FOL model is organised around them. The Eduversal framework has no SLO aspect: D1 covers vision and mission, D4 covers achievement, but the explicit SLO link between them is absent. A school preparing for CIS or WASC must author SLOs separately; the appraisal will not prompt for them.

Financial and facilities management. CIS 8 and WASC Category D both assess financial sustainability, facilities and resourcing as institutional quality. The Eduversal appraisal is academically scoped: it touches resources only where they bear on teaching (D3) or culture (D5). Governance of finance sits with the Yayasan and is outside the appraisal.

Cycle length and independence. CIS and WASC run multi-year cycles with teams drawn from independent peer schools. The Eduversal cycle is annual and the team is drawn from the network's own specialists. This is a considered trade-off — it buys frequency, subject expertise and continuity, at the cost of the external independence an accreditation body requires. The appraisal is internal quality assurance, not an accreditation simulation.

Outcome type. Accreditation yields a binary decision (accredited or not). The appraisal yields a School Development Rating, explicitly a development indicator and not a ranking. A school rated Developing is not "failing accreditation"; it has named priorities and a supervisor assigned to them.

content.text: Where a school is actively pursuing CIS or WASC accreditation, Section 18 (Accreditation Toolkit) governs. This section explains how appraisal evidence feeds that process; it does not replace the accreditation body's own self-study instrument.
This section is a mapping between documents that change independently, so it goes stale silently. Three maintenance rules:

items: When the appraisal framework changes (a domain renamed, an aspect added or retired), update 24.2 and re-check every mapping table. The framework's own file is Central Hub/resources/school-appraisal-framework.json, mirrored byte-identically into Academic Hub.

When an external framework publishes a new edition, verify the mapping before changing the edition number. A new CIS or WASC edition can renumber or merge domains, which silently invalidates rows here.

The frameworkAnchors block on each domain in school-appraisal-framework.json carries the machine-readable version of these mappings, and the appraisal page renders them. Source of truth is this section; the JSON follows it. If the two disagree, this section is right and the JSON needs correcting — not the reverse.
